bearings.paper_claim: Lazy greedy (Algorithm 2) loses no solution quality because stale marginals upper-bound current ones. Speedups were about 3.5-7x fewer evaluations on 46 sensors (temperature) and 30-38x on 357 sensors (traffic) at 50 percent failure. The Lemma 6 data-dependent bound was tighter than the worst-case bound in the sensor runs.
bearings.paper_location: Sec 4.4 p.9 (intro summary 4 to 40x); Lemma 6 Eq.13 p.11; Sec 10.1.2 p.30; Sec 10.1.3 pp.31-32
bearings.system_side: Heap-based lazy greedy over $500 chunks in optimize.py re-queues a member only when its marginal is stale. dd_bound sums each member's current next-chunk marginal times the chunks left in its PMAX headroom, within BUDGET, and is computed only under the fixed-state certificate. The code comment calls exact greedy optimality stronger than the 1-1/e floor.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Carries over in the deterministic fixed-state case where per-member chunk marginals are non-increasing, which the code's concavity check tests. It does not carry over once modeled conversions fire; the code then withholds the certificate. The code citation Golovin-Krause JAIR 11 Lemma 5.3 / A.9 does not match this text copy, which has Lemma 6 Eq.13 and Lemma 37 for costs.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers and both speedup ranges confirmed at the cited pages. Code paths confirmed by reading. Only the code comment's lemma citation is wrong. This is a second reading of the same code, not an independent reproduction, so DE-062 still applies.

bearings.paper_claim: Theorem 5's (1-1/e) bound compares with the best adaptive policy and needs observed outcomes, an adaptive monotone submodular objective and a known prior (Def 2-3 p.8; Thm 5 p.11). Treasure-hunting instances with strong synergies fall outside the class (Sec 3.4 p.9). Theorem 26 shows no O(|E|^(1-eps/beta)) approximation for a constructed treasure-hunting family of pointwise-modular instances unless PH = Sigma_2^P (Sec 12 p.33).
bearings.paper_location: Def 2-3 p.8; Thm 5 p.11; Sec 3.4 p.9; Sec 12 and Thm 26 p.33; proof App 15.7 pp.57-60
bearings.system_side: Nothing is observed (observations is an empty list). When cumulative CU dollars cross the deterministic DTHRESH threshold, the member is banked as won, the stance matrix shifts and the queue is rebuilt. The run is labelled modeled_threshold_replanning with guarantee kind none.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper supports the refusal to claim a certificate in conversion mode, since a threshold jump can make a later chunk's marginal rise. Softened scope: Theorem 26 is a hardness result for one constructed family, not for every objective lacking adaptive submodularity. Sec 12 frames it more broadly, but the proof covers only that family.
bearings.verifier_note: Code behaviour confirmed by reading: no observations, conversion labels and the none guarantee. The analyst's phrasing that without the property Theorem 26 gives no O(|E|^(1-eps)) approximation overstates the theorem. Rewritten as scoped to the constructed family.

bearings.paper_claim: Stochastic submodular maximization with independent item states (failure types) and a monotone submodular objective: greedy obtains (1-1/e) of the best adaptive policy (Thm 16, generalizing Asadpour et al. 2008). Robustness to a misspecified prior is shown for a multiplicative error condition with alpha = d/c (Sec 4.3).
bearings.paper_location: Thm 16 p.17; Sec 4.3 p.9; known-prior assumption in Sec 2.1 main text near p.4
bearings.system_side: Each lobbied seed activates independently with probability gate(n) = max(0.15, seed_prob x SGATE[tier]). Draws use a dedicated CRN key range offset by 2^62. SGATE runs from 1.00 (Highly Persuadable) to 0.35 (Opponent) as design constants; unlisted tiers default to 0.85.
bearings.code_ref: fec/moneyball_core.py:626-630 (gate and SGATE table); fec/engine/budget_frontier.py:128; fec/engine/per_topic_coalition.py:107
bearings.transfer_conditions: The structure matches: independent per-seed Bernoulli take-up over a spread function. The guarantee also needs spread given activated seeds to be monotone submodular, which is not shown for this competitive kernel, and needs known take-up probabilities. SGATE and seed_prob are unestimated, so the known-prior assumption fails.
bearings.verifier_note: Thm 16 product prior, monotone objective and (1-1/e) confirmed. Gate formula, SGATE values and the 2^62 offset confirmed by reading. The analyst's footnote 2 citation is not the source of the known-prior statement; the main text in Sec 2.1 states it.

bearings.paper_claim: Greedy guarantees assume exact or alpha-approximate marginal evaluation; sampled marginals give only additive error (Sec 5 p.11, bound with epsilon). The adaptive IC result (Thm 19 p.21) covers a single cascade with full-adoption feedback; the myopic-feedback version was retracted with a 3-node counterexample (Sec 8.2.1 p.23).
bearings.system_side: Lazy greedy picks up to 60 seeds (MAXSEEDS default 60). Each marginal is a 20-draw CRN Monte Carlo estimate (MC=20) on a two-colour first-to-reach cascade with money-mobilized bystanders. Marginals are clamped at zero and multiplied by a per-candidate factor fac: REPFAC times lev for contest candidates, 1.0 for defend candidates, and lev for all others. The knee is read from the raw path.
bearings.transfer_conditions: No Golovin-Krause guarantee carries over as built. Marginals are sampled, selection uses fac-weighted marginals rather than the reported spread, and the kernel is competitive. The zero clamp signals that sampled spread is not monotone. The frontier is a non-adaptive heuristic.
bearings.verifier_note: Corrected fac description: the code uses lev, not c, for non-contest non-defend candidates. Verified MC=20, MAXSEEDS=60, the zero clamp and sampled marginals. The knee-input claim rests on the KNEE_RAW name and was not traced line by line.

bearings.paper_claim: Near-optimality comes from greedy selection that conditions each pick on what has been selected or observed. For deterministic priors the notion reduces to classical submodularity, so Nemhauser et al. (1-1/e) applies (Sec 3.1-3.2 pp.6-8; Thm 5 p.11; Conclusions p.36).
bearings.paper_location: Sec 3.1-3.2 pp.6-8; Thm 5 p.11; Conclusions p.36
bearings.system_side: Coalition allocator ranks the top-45 neutral candidates by singleton marginals spread({n}) minus base, splits the budget by water-fill with a per-member cap and no sequential conditioning, then reports the joint spread of the funded set. A comment asserts spread is submodular. The flip allocator is an exact heap-based greedy over pflip chunks.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Flip allocator: with fixed-state separable concave pflip, greedy is exact, so the paper adds nothing. Coalition allocator: the singleton-marginal proportional split is not greedy, so no submodular guarantee applies even if spread were submodular; reporting joint spread is the right diagnostic. Submodularity of the bystander-filtered competitive kernel is unverified.
bearings.verifier_note: Confirmed singleton marginals, top-45 cut, water-fill with cap, joint-spread report, flip greedy heap and the submodularity comment. The 2M dollar budget in the analyst text was not checked against the BUDGET default.

bearings.paper_claim: The (1-1/e) greedy guarantee holds for the monotone submodular objective greedy maximizes (Sec 3.1-3.2 pp.6-8). Under IC with full-adoption feedback, observing which asks succeed keeps adaptive submodularity (Thm 19 p.21).
bearings.system_side: budgetRecruit maximizes probabilistic coverage cov = 1 minus product of (1 minus p), which is monotone submodular. When a target is set, each candidate marginal g is multiplied by (1 + 2 dT[c]), and the code comment still claims the (1-1/e) guarantee for reported reach. No ask outcome is observed.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Without a target the classical guarantee holds for reach. With a target the selection score is not the marginal of any fixed submodular function, so the (1-1/e) comment overstates the claim. An adaptive version would need recruit outcomes fed back, which is not built.
bearings.verifier_note: Template code and comment confirmed by reading. Paper support confirmed. The analyst's statement that no ask outcome is observed is consistent with the template.

summary_issues: Verified against the text: Thm 5 (1-1/e with alpha), Lemma 6 Eq.13, Thm 13 and 14 squared-log and single-log factors, Thm 15 4 alpha, Thm 16, Thm 19, Thm 26 O(|E|^(1-eps/beta)) with PH = Sigma_2^P, the 3.5-7x and 30-38x speedups with 46 and 357 sensors at 50 percent failure, the pointwise counterexample (1/2 vs 1), and the myopic counterexample (eps vs 1).

Summary overstates Theorem 26: it proves hardness for a constructed treasure-hunting family of pointwise-modular instances (Sec 12 p.33; proof App 15.7), not for every objective lacking adaptive submodularity. Scope should be stated.

Code comment at fec/engine/optimize.py:108 cites Golovin-Krause JAIR 11 Lemma 5.3 / A.9. This text copy has no Lemma 5.3; the bound is Lemma 6 Eq.13 (Sec 5.1.1 p.11) and the cost version is Lemma 37. Citation should be fixed in the code, not in this paper's record.
